title: Oxford Economics Acquires FrontierView
gist: Oxford Economics acquired strategic-insights firm FrontierView to pair its macroeconomic forecasting with advisory-led, C-suite-facing corporate insight, notably gaining genuine specialist depth in healthcare for the first time.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics has acquired FrontierView, a strategic insights firm that provides market monitoring, industry data, and executive advisory services to corporate decision-makers worldwide.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Consolidation in the economic/strategic advisory space signals demand from corporate clients for integrated macro-plus-strategy offerings rather than piecing together separate vendors.
insights.quote: Oxford Economics has acquired FrontierView, a premier strategic insights firm providing market monitoring, industry data, and executive advisory services to corporate decision-makers worldwide.

insights.claim: FrontierView was founded in 2008, originally under the name Frontier Strategy Group, and helps global business leaders evaluate market conditions, inform strategic planning, and drive international expansion, with specialist depth in healthcare alongside broader corporate advisory work.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: The rebrand history and healthcare specialization are the specific assets Oxford Economics is buying, not just generic market research capacity.
insights.quote: Founded in 2008 (originally as Frontier Strategy Group), FrontierView helps global business leaders evaluate market conditions, inform strategic planning, and drive international expansion, with specialist depth in healthcare alongside its broader corporate advisory work.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics CEO Innes McFee framed the acquisition as combining FrontierView's strategic insights with Oxford Economics' macroeconomic foundation to give clients a more complete offering for strategy and growth decisions.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Signals Oxford Economics' strategic direction is moving from pure macro forecasting toward applied, advisory-led corporate strategy consulting.
insights.quote: This acquisition is about unlocking the power of economics to drive real strategic advantage for our clients... By bringing together FrontierView’s strategic insights with our macroeconomic foundation, we’re giving our clients a more complete offering to inform strategy and drive growth in an increasingly complex world.

insights.claim: The combined Oxford Economics-FrontierView offering pairs globally consistent macroeconomic forecasting with senior, advisory-led insight that translates directly into C-suite decision-making, giving clients a single joined-up view instead of needing to piece macro and strategic insight together from separate sources.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Positions the merged firm as a one-stop competitor to both pure macro forecasting houses and standalone strategy advisory firms, raising switching costs for clients who previously used multiple vendors.
insights.quote: Clients gain a single, joined-up view rather than needing to piece macro and strategic insight together from separate sources, backed by a deeper bench of research and a broader global network than either firm offered alone.
insights.locator: Together, the two firms bring clients

insights.claim: Oxford Economics states this acquisition gives it genuine, specialist depth in healthcare for the first time, an area where it previously lacked dedicated expertise despite its broad macroeconomic coverage.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: An admission that a firm covering 200 countries and 100 industrial sectors still had a healthcare capability gap suggests sector-specific advisory depth doesn't automatically follow from broad macro coverage, and points to healthcare as the near-term growth focus for the combined firm.
insights.quote: particularly in healthcare, where this acquisition gives us genuine, specialist depth for the first time
insights.locator: We see this as a natural fit

insights.claim: Oxford Economics describes itself as the world's foremost independent economic advisory firm, covering over 200 countries, 100 industrial sectors, and 8,000 cities and regions.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Establishes the scale of the acquiring firm's existing footprint, the base onto which FrontierView's advisory and healthcare capabilities are being layered.
insights.quote: Covering over 200 countries, 100 industrial sectors, and 8,000 cities and regions, we provide rigorous economic analysis and forecasting to empower leaders to make faster, more confident decisions in an uncertain world.
